A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StoryGPT-V research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support matching the methods, equations, tables, figures, and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on FlintstonesSV and PororoSV, component ablations, human evaluation, computational measurements, and qualitative story-generation results, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, human evaluation, computational measurements, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two-stage method is unchanged: character-augmented embeddings and segmentation-guided attention train Char-LDM, followed by LLM alignment for reference resolution. The architecture, losses, token mappings, and inference procedure remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use FlintstonesSV and PororoSV with the same referential-caption extensions, long-story tests, and multimodal continuation example. The added preprocessing disclosure does not introduce a new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 10 retain StoryDALL-E, LDM, and Story-LDM as comparators. The human and long-story comparisons against Story-LDM and the qualitative DALL-E 3 comparison in Figure 9 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated splits, metrics, training budgets, frame counts, and human-study design are unchanged. Appendix D.1 newly documents super-resolution preprocessing, but v1 states no conflicting preprocessing setting and v3 reports no protocol revision or rerun; this is additional disclosure under D1.

E4.justification: The attention, feature-fusion, interleaving, alignment-target, image-token-count, and OPT/Llama2 ablations are retained. Long-story analyses, attention visualizations, metric comparisons, and qualitative cases are unchanged; Figure 7 restyles an existing example.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing. Both versions retain the same point estimates and human evaluation using three unique workers per story pair.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains StoryGPT-V's referential FlintstonesSV character accuracy of 87.96 and FID of 21.71; Table 2 retains PororoSV values of 36.06 and 19.56. Figure 7 retains the same frames and narrative continuation.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 are identical, as is the character-replacement pseudocode in Algorithm 1. No assumptions, derivations, theoretical results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reference resolution, character consistency, image quality, and efficient story generation. Figure 7's added novelty sentence reiterates multimodal continuation and priority claims already present in Section 4.5 and Appendix A.

C2.justification: Explanations of attention guidance, context retention, evaluation metrics, and the small OPT/Llama2 difference are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitation concerning imperfect replication of visual details when aligning through semantic embeddings.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly states that the datasets are enhanced from 128x128 to 512x512 using super-resolution before training and evaluating all models, and identifies the checkpoint through a link. The project-page pointer is updated and the anonymous source-code pointer is replaced by a named GitHub repository. Other implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 60 numbered references are unchanged. Figure 7's revised priority wording repeats the existing positioning of StoryGPT-V as supporting both story visualization and multimodal narrative continuation.

P1.justification: The title gains the prefix 'StoryGPT-V:', the webpage footnote drops 'anonymous', and Figure 7's caption is expanded. A short preprocessing passage is added to Appendix D.1; the section order and overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 7 gains green and orange dashed outlines and corresponding caption colors to distinguish story visualization from continuation. Its images are retained. Local text reflow accompanies the expanded caption and implementation details; the other figures and table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The super-resolution disclosure and checkpoint pointer in Appendix D.1 resolve a specific gap in documenting how the benchmark images were prepared. Updated project/code pointers and clearer Figure 7 annotations also improve usability. These are limited improvements to reproducibility and presentation; the methods and empirical evidence are retained.
